name: Enumclaw
headline: Enumclaw: a plateau town at the foot of the Cascades, where the Chinook Scenic Byway begins.
lede: Enumclaw sits on the Enumclaw Plateau in southeast King County, against the Cascade foothills, with farmland on three sides and SR 410 heading east toward Mount Rainier. This guide covers getting around, parks and the nearby state parks, schools, everyday errands, housing figures, and what’s nearby, with a source for every fact.

notes: Land area: the Census Bureau and the Wikipedia infobox give 5.17 square miles, while the Wikipedia article text gives 4.27. This guide uses the Census figure.

Home values: Wikipedia lists a median home value of $753,000 without a clear source or date; this guide uses the Census Bureau’s 2020–2024 median owner-occupied value of $524,600, which is a survey estimate of what owners say their homes are worth, not a sale-price figure.

Enumclaw Expo Center size: Visit Enumclaw and Wikipedia say 72 acres; the city’s February 2025 parks chapter lists the Expo Center at 55 acres. This guide uses 72 acres from the Expo’s own tourism page and flags the difference.
The city’s parks chapter lists a city park total of 150.58 acres, but its listed park acreages add to about 116.6, so this guide gives the number of parks and individual park sizes, not a total.
St. Elizabeth Hospital replaced the town’s earlier hospital in 2011; Becker’s calls it Enumclaw Regional Hospital and Wikipedia calls it Enumclaw Community Hospital, so the old name is left out.

Name meaning: Wikipedia traces “Enumclaw” to a Sahaptin word meaning “he who makes noise,” and notes the City of Enumclaw gives “thundering noise.” The guide mentions only that the town is named for nearby Enumclaw Mountain.
The Buckley Wikipedia page still describes the SR 410 White River Bridge as closed; WSDOT reports it reopened October 17, 2025, so this guide follows WSDOT.

Bus service: King County Metro’s own schedule pages could not be read for this draft, so bus details come from the Wikipedia Auburn station page. Confirm current routes with King County Metro before publishing.
Census housing and commute figures are 2020–2024 American Community Survey estimates, not a single-year count.

chapters.title: Getting around and commutes
chapters.intro: Three state routes meet in Enumclaw, and SR 410 continues east into the mountains. Census figures put the mean travel time to work for Enumclaw residents at 33.0 minutes (2020–2024).
items: SR 410 runs 107.44 miles from SR 167 in Sumner to US 12 in Naches, passing through Enumclaw, Federation Forest State Park and Mount Rainier National Park over Cayuse and Chinook passes.

A 14.82-mile state highway from an interchange with SR 18 in Auburn to SR 410 in Enumclaw. It follows the White River along the Auburn–Enumclaw Road and passes through the Muckleshoot Indian Reservation.
SR 169 to Maple Valley and Renton

The Maple Valley Highway runs 25.26 miles north from Enumclaw through Black Diamond and Maple Valley to Renton. It crosses the Green River gorge on the Kummer Bridge (officially the Dan Evans Bridge), about 155 feet above the water.

The SR 410 steel truss bridge over the White River, built in 1949, connects Enumclaw and Buckley and carries an average of 22,099 vehicles a day. It has a 14-foot clearance, and WSDOT added an over-height warning system in 2026.
An over-height vehicle struck the White River Bridge on August 18, 2025, damaging several beams. WSDOT reopened it on Friday, October 17, 2025, ahead of schedule.

The SR 410 Chinook Pass and SR 123 Cayuse Pass segments through Mount Rainier National Park close for winter. In 2026 they were scheduled to reopen by 8 a.m. on May 22, in time for Memorial Day weekend.

King County Metro bus and dial-a-ride routes connect Enumclaw with Auburn station, which has 13 weekday Sounder S Line round trips, about 35 minutes to Seattle and 28 minutes to Tacoma, and 633 parking spaces.

chapters.title: Parks and outdoors
chapters.intro: City parks, a regional trail and several state parks along the White and Green rivers are within reach of town. The city lists 22 city-owned parks in its February 2025 parks chapter.
items: The 22 city-owned parks include 7 mini-parks, 9 neighborhood parks and 6 community parks. Among the larger ones: Mahler Park (30 acres, undeveloped), Boise Creek Park (19.3 acres), Sportsman Park (12.86 acres) and Farmers Park (9.7 acres, with a disc golf course).
The city-owned Enumclaw Golf Course covers 188 acres with 18 holes and is leased to a private operator. The Enumclaw Aquatic Center has a 4,956-square-foot pool in a 13,540-square-foot building.

A mostly paved trail from Puyallup through Orting, South Prairie and Buckley to Enumclaw. Its 572-foot White River bridge, which cost $16 million, opened in October 2024 and linked the trail into Enumclaw.
A 619-acre old-growth forest that SR 410 parallels along the White River east of Enumclaw.

At 49201 Highway 410 E: about 12 miles of easy to moderate trails through forest and wetlands. The Catherine T. Montgomery Interpretive Center is open Friday through Sunday in June through August. A storm-damaged trail to the riverside picnic area was closed when checked.

A 432-foot U.S. Army Corps of Engineers flood-control dam on the White River, finished in 1948, a few miles southeast of Enumclaw. Its day-use recreation area has picnic facilities, interpretive exhibits and ten miles of hiking trails.
A day-use park on Deep Lake near the Green River Gorge, at 36921 Veazie Cumberland Road, with an easy 1.4-mile loop trail around the lake. Open 8 a.m. to dusk year-round.
A 503-acre park with more than 3 miles of Green River shoreline near Black Diamond. Its name comes from a methane pocket struck by a coal test hole in the early 1900s.
About 320 acres with roughly 2 miles of Green River shoreline, camping and about 3 miles of trails. Experienced paddlers can raft and kayak the expert-level Green River Gorge.

chapters.title: Schools
chapters.intro: Enumclaw is in the Enumclaw School District #216, which covers about 456 square miles. Boundaries change; confirm school assignment with the district for any specific address.
items: The district serves the cities of Enumclaw and Black Diamond plus several unincorporated communities, with 4,225 students as of November 2023.
Five elementary schools: Black Diamond, Byron Kibler, Southwood, Sunrise and Westwood. The district also runs a Birth to Five Center.
Two middle schools, Enumclaw and Thunder Mountain, and one high school, Enumclaw High School.
Because of growth in Black Diamond, the district set a boundary in 2022–2023 assigning parts of the Ten Trails area to Westwood Elementary.
The district office is at 2929 McDougall Ave, Enumclaw; call (360) 802-7100 to confirm which schools serve a specific address.
Green River’s first branch campus, opened in 1996 at 1414 Griffin Avenue, offers credit and continuing education classes, proctoring and room rentals.

chapters.title: Everyday errands
chapters.intro: Downtown, the hospital, the library and the Expo Center are all in town, and the city runs more of its own utilities than most.
items: At 1455 Battersby Avenue, part of Virginia Mason Franciscan Health, with a 24/7 emergency department, a Family Birth Center, inpatient and surgical care, imaging and a walk-in lab.
The current hospital opened February 2, 2011, as a 25-bed critical access hospital with private rooms and a rooftop helicopter pad, replacing the town’s earlier hospital.
Part of the King County Library System, at 1700 1st Street at Railroad Avenue.
The first library opened in City Hall in 1923. The current 10,541-square-foot building opened in 1991, and the library joined KCLS in 2012.

A 72-acre site, formerly the King County Fairgrounds, with multi-use buildings, arenas and grass midways. King County transferred it to the city in 2006, and since July 1, 2015, a nonprofit, the Enumclaw Expo and Events Association, has run it.
More than 180,000 people a year come for events such as the King County Fair, the Scottish Highland Games, the Olympic Kennel Club Dog Show and the Enumclaw Pro-Rodeo.
The city runs its own garbage, water, stormwater and sewer utilities and owns its natural gas utility, one of two city-owned gas utilities in Washington.
City offices are at 1339 Griffin Avenue; the main number is 360-825-3591.

chapters.title: Housing and neighborhoods
chapters.intro: Enumclaw is a compact city ringed by farmland. The figures below are from the Census Bureau and the city’s comprehensive plan.
items: Owner-occupied housing rate 74.3%, median owner-occupied home value $524,600 and median gross rent $1,954 (Census, 2020–2024).
The city’s housing appendix notes that historically only detached single-family homes have been built in the city, and only 7 accessory dwelling units were built from 2018 to 2023.

The comprehensive plan sets a target of 1,057 new housing units and 202 emergency housing beds through 2044, against an estimated capacity of about 2,016 units including projects already in the pipeline.
Farm preservation land surrounds the city on three sides, with protected forest to the east. Enumclaw counts 16 Grade “A” dairy farms.
Downtown is a mix of small local boutiques and non-chain restaurants; summer brings the Sidewalk Street Fair in the third week of July and Sundays on Cole.
The Enumclaw Plateau formed from a Mount Rainier lahar about 5,700 years ago. Frank and Mary Stevenson homesteaded the town site in 1879, and hops gave way to dairy farming after crop failures.

Summers typically run about 5°F warmer than Seattle and winters about 5°F colder, with 6 to 8 inches of snow in a typical year. Enumclaw recorded the state’s highest wind, 74 mph, in the November 2024 bomb cyclone.

chapters.title: What’s nearby
chapters.intro: Enumclaw sits at the King–Pierce county line, with the White River between it and Buckley, and the mountains straight east.
items: Enumclaw is the gateway to Mount Rainier National Park and the Crystal Mountain ski area.
An 85-mile All-American Road from Enumclaw over Chinook Pass to the Naches valley, about three hours of driving past the glacier-fed White River and Mount Rainier views.
A Pierce County city of 5,114 (2020 census) on the south side of the White River, which forms the King–Pierce county line.
A Pierce County city of 22,487 (2020 census) split by SR 410, which links it to the rest of the Seattle area and the northeast side of Mount Rainier.
A city of 4,697 (2020 census), incorporated February 19, 1959, that grew up around coal mining starting in the 1880s.
SR 164 runs 14.82 miles along the White River from Enumclaw to SR 18 in Auburn.
SR 169 crosses the gorge on the Kummer Bridge, about 155 feet above the Green River, on the way to Black Diamond and Maple Valley.
The Foothills Trail links Enumclaw with Buckley, South Prairie, Orting and Puyallup, with frequent Mount Rainier views.
